claims.statement: The CBAM definitive regime applies from 1 January 2026; importers above a single 50-tonne mass threshold for covered goods must seek authorized-declarant status, declare embedded emissions, buy certificates, and surrender the required amount annually.

Because emissions evidence originates at non-EU installations while quantities originate in customs systems, reconciliation and supplier chasing form a real handoff problem for importers without specialist staff.
The count and service spend of threshold-crossing Polish SMEs and mid-market importers are unknown.

contrary_evidence: The 50-tonne threshold materially reduces the small-importer market compared with the transitional regime.
Customs brokers, accounting firms, verifiers, and enterprise software vendors may bundle the same work.
Regulatory simplifications, default values, and scope changes can reduce or reshape the manual evidence burden.

economics.acquisition_route: Integrate the offer into customs-broker intake: when covered CN codes cumulatively approach the threshold, the broker's workflow automatically quotes a fixed evidence-onboarding package. This makes distribution event-driven and gives the broker a service it can resell without building an emissions team.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Multilingual supplier-response playbooks, customs-to-facility reconciliation controls, exception handling, registry integration, and a reliable verifier handoff reduce cycle time. Embedded broker workflows and execution quality compound; supplier data alone are not treated as a moat.
fingerprint.customer: Polish and CEE importers above the applicable mass threshold for iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilizers, hydrogen, or electricity, plus indirect customs representatives serving many such importers.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Integrate the offer into customs-broker intake: when covered CN codes cumulatively approach the threshold, the broker's workflow automatically quotes a fixed evidence-onboarding package. This makes distribution event-driven and gives the broker a service it can resell without building an emissions team.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Map customs lines to covered goods, monitor threshold exposure, send multilingual facility templates, validate completeness and units, reconcile quantities to declarations, preserve evidence, and export a registry-ready workpaper. Accredited verification and legal opinions stay with qualified third parties rather than being implied by the data service.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The importer pays an onboarding fee and monthly retainer by supplier/facility count, with a fixed per-exception fee when missing or inconsistent evidence requires resolution; an indirect customs representative can buy the workflow white-label per client.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A covered purchase order or customs entry pushes annual tonnage over the threshold, a supplier fails to return installation-level emissions data, or the importer must prepare its annual declaration and certificate position.

founder_fit: Excellent fit with data pipelines, reconciliation, business analysis, AI-assisted document handling, and FMCG supply-chain familiarity.
Can start part-time as a narrow productized operation without physical assets or public-facing content.
The founder must avoid using employer-confidential supplier data and must define a strict boundary from regulated verification or legal advice.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: CBAM Supplier-Evidence Operations for CEE Importers
uncertainties: Number of addressable importers by Polish customs broker and average supplier/facility complexity.
Supplier response rate and time per exception once definitive-method data are requested.
Professional-liability insurance and reviewer costs needed for a credible service.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: With client permission, process three months of anonymized customs lines from five importers or one broker, identify covered exposure and request sample data from ten suppliers. Sell at least two fixed-fee onboarding packages and measure labor per facility; stop if buyers prefer broker-bundled compliance at a price below sustainable delivery cost.
